We have deep experience in the strategy, design, delivery and assurance of large-scale transformation across financial services, energy, commodities, utilities, telecoms and government. Our people become trusted advisors, independent of any technology provider, and deliver real value for our clients.</p> <p>AI is changing how organisations work, compete and invest, and it’s changing architecture with it. Our clients need architects who can cut through the hype, turn ambition into practical action and create value without losing control of cost, risk or complexity.</p> <p>In our Architecture practice we bring the right balance of innovation, pace and control to technology-enabled change. We work on our clients’ most complex and highest-return challenges. Commodity or ivory-tower architecture isn’t where we play.</p> <p>As a Manager, you’ll lead architecture work, use AI to raise the pace and quality of what we deliver, and play an active part in growing our business. You’ll spot opportunities, shape compelling work and build relationships that last well beyond a single engagement.</p> <p> </p> <h3><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142);"><span data-contrast="none">What you will be doing</span></span></h3> <p> </p> <p><strong>Lead architecture that delivers real value</strong></p> <p>You’ll lead architecture work that turns strategy into practical change. That means owning architecture engagements and workstreams, shaping target architectures and roadmaps, and helping clients make better decisions about where to invest, what to simplify and how to manage risk.</p> <ul> <li>Lead engagements with clear ownership of scope, quality, outcomes and client relationships</li> <li>Help organisations improve their architecture functions, operating models and governance</li> <li>Communicate complex ideas clearly, from delivery teams through to CTOs and CIOs</li> </ul> <p><strong>Help clients navigate AI-enabled change</strong></p> <p>You’ll help clients move from interest in AI to safe, valuable adoption. We’ll look to you to cut through the noise, design for change and make sure AI-enabled solutions have the foundations they need: data, integration, security, identity, governance and clear ownership.</p> <ul> <li>Shape AI-ready architectures that balance innovation, pace and control</li> <li>Help clients move beyond disconnected pilots to reusable services, governed delivery and measurable value</li> <li>Use AI tools to speed up research, analysis, option development and architecture artefacts, with strong quality assurance throughout</li> </ul> <p><strong>Create and convert commercial opportunities</strong></p> <p>You’ll play an active part in growing our business. That means spotting where we can help, shaping work that clients value and building the confidence to convert good conversations into deliverable opportunities.</p> <ul> <li>Qualify opportunities through delivery, market insight and trusted relationships</li> <li>Shape proposals, statements of work, team shapes and commercial models with discipline</li> <li>Build architecture propositions that match our growth priorities and the challenges our clients face</li> </ul> <p><strong>Lead people and build our capability</strong></p> <p>You’ll help build the kind of team people want to work in and clients want to work with. You’ll coach others, share what works and help us turn individual expertise into reusable capability across the practice.</p> <ul> <li>Lead mixed Baringa and client teams with clear expectations and a strong coaching mindset</li> <li>Coach colleagues on effective and responsible use of AI</li> <li>Help grow the practice through training, thought leadership, reusable assets and recruitment</li> </ul> <p> </p> <h3><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142);"> </span><br><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142);"><span data-contrast="none">Your skills and experience</span> </span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559738":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></h3> <ul> <li>Experience leading architecture work within complex technology-enabled change, with a strong delivery focus</li> <li>Experience in both enterprise and solution architecture, translating strategy into deliverable target architectures and roadmaps, and designing and assuring solutions to achieve it</li> <li>Broad experience across architecture domains (business, application, integration, data, infrastructure and security), with deep expertise in at least one</li> <li>Cloud experience across XaaS offerings, with knowledge of cloud-native services and how to use them in cloud and hybrid solutions</li> <li>A practical understanding of AI and the architecture considerations needed to adopt it safely and at scale. Hands-on AI design experience is a bonus, not a must</li> <li>Experience contributing to proposals, bids or account growth, and the commercial awareness to shape work that is valuable and deliverable</li> <li>The ability to take ownership of projects and teams, sell work and deliver results</li> <li>Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain the complex in simple terms, concisely and with clarity</li> <li>Experience managing stakeholders from C-suite through to engineering, and a desire to build lasting relationships</li> <li>A collaborative style, real curiosity and a genuine interest in helping others grow </li> </ul> <h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142);"><span data-contrast="none">What a career at Baringa will give you</span> </span></h2> <h3><br><span data-contrast="none"><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142);">Putting</span> </span><span data-contrast="none"><span style="color: rgb(208, 0, 111);">People</span> </span><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142);"><span data-contrast="none">First.</span> </span></h3> <h3><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142);"><span data-contrast="none">Baringa is a People First company and wellbeing is at the forefront of our culture. title: Senior Supply Specialist - UK
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.</p></div><p><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The UK Operations Team is responsible for delivering Waymo service across UK cities. This role works closely with Product, Operations Partnerships, Engineering, Global Operations, Ops Planning, Finance, Safety, Policy and business partners.</span></p> <p><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">We are seeking a confident, decisive, and results-oriented leader to join our team as a Supply Operations Manager. This role demands an individual who thrives in fast-paced, dynamic environments, excels at managing cross-functional teams, and is committed to driving operational success and market excellence for our autonomous ride-hailing service. You'll foster strong partnerships, champion continuous improvement, and leverage data analytics to monitor market health, identify trends, and implement proactive strategies to balance demand and supply, ultimately driving innovation and long-term success.</span></p> <p><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">In this hybrid role, you will report to the <strong>Country Lead within the European Market Operations Team.</strong></span></p> <p><strong>You will:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strategic Leadership (Partner Support/Management): Strategic and decisive leadership to manage and optimize daily partner operations, fostering a high-performance culture emphasizing collaboration and accountability, escalating product issues while supporting partner multi-facility operations (partner results) to ensure strict adherence to all safety, compliance, and regulatory protocols.</li> <li>Commercialization: Primary liaison to support internal stakeholders in expanding the market by providing guidance and expertise, communicating with all stakeholders to ensure alignment, monitoring progress, identifying potential issues, and developing contingency plans to ensure the success and sustainability of the market scale.</li> <li>Supply & Demand Planning: Manage Supply & Demand Planning by ensuring that staffing levels align with operational needs and in-service supply.</li> <li>Continuous Improvement: Must be continuously monitoring and improving processes, systems, and performance metrics to drive efficiency and productivity, and reduce costs.</li> <li>Co-Lead Market Expansion: Strategically expand the market by executing innovative initiatives with partners, leveraging data insights, and applying critical thinking to identify opportunities and resolve challenges effectively.</li> <li>Build Collaborative Partnerships: Build and maintain strong partnerships across the company and with partners, ensuring alignment with organizational standards, goals, and a shared commitment to success.</li> <li>Drive Sustainable Outcomes: Serve as a trusted leader with a continuous improvement mindset, consistently monitoring and enhancing processes, systems, and performance metrics to drive operational excellence, strengthen stakeholder alignment, and deliver measurable, sustainable results, all while boosting efficiency, productivity, and reducing costs.</li> <li>Maximize Market Profitability: Manage departmental budgets, identifying and implementing cost-saving initiatives, and monitoring key performance indicators to effectively allocate resources and ensure all operational initiatives align with financial parameters and organizational goals.</li> </ul> <p><strong>You have:</strong></p> <ul> <li>10+ years of experience in operations management, preferably managing daily operations in a fast-paced environment in fleet management, transportation, or logistics, with a deep understanding of safety.</li> <li>Bachelor's degree, or in lieu of a degree, an additional 6+ years of work experience in a combination of program management, business operations, strategy consulting, planning, or equivalent fields.</li> <li>Excellent leadership skills, including the ability to motivate & lead by influence partner teams, develop and execute strategies, and drive performance improvement.</li> <li>Ability to deal with multiple conflicting priorities and stakeholder issues while driving towards pragmatic decisions/actions.</li> <li>Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to identify and address performance issues proactively, preferably using data analytics tools and reporting software to track key metrics and performance trends.</li> <li>Strong communication and presentation skills showcasing an ability to influence people to contribute to continuous improvement of operations.</li> </ul> <p><strong>We prefer:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience in Ride-Hail & Transportation: Direct experience in the ride-hailing or broader transportation industry is a significant plus.</li> <li>Data-Driven Decision Making: Proficiency in leveraging data analytics and reporting tools to monitor market health and inform strategic decisions is essential. Experience with SQL and data mining is highly preferred.</li> <li>Operational Management Experience: A background in general operations management, vendor management in addition to the minimum requirements, would be beneficial.</li> <li>Continuous Improvement Mindset: A demonstrated history of identifying and implementing process improvements to increase efficiency and reduce costs.</li> <li>Strategic & Decisive Leadership: The ability to provide clear, strategic leadership and make quick decisions in a fast-paced environment.</li> </ul><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><span style="font-weight: 400;">The expected base salary range for this full-time position is listed below. title: Sales Operations Business Partner
description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role We’re looking for a Sales Operations Business Partner to sit between our sales leadership and the systems, data, and processes that run the revenue engine. You’ll help the sales team understand where deals stand, where revenue is coming from, and where it’s at risk. You’ll own how we track pipeline, report on performance, and build the dashboards leaders rely on to make decisions. This is a role for someone who thinks in business outcomes first and uses data and tools as the means to get there. What you’ll do Own pipeline management processes, including stage definitions, forecasting cadence, and hygiene standards, and work with sales managers to keep the pipeline accurate. Build and maintain regular sales reporting covering bookings, pipeline coverage, conversion rates, win/loss, and rep and team performance. Design, build, and maintain dashboards that give leadership and frontline managers a clear view of performance against targets. Act as a business partner to sales leaders: understand their priorities, translate them into operational requirements, and bring data-backed recommendations to planning and business reviews. Support forecasting and quarterly business reviews by preparing the data, challenging assumptions, and flagging risks early. Own day-to-day administration and configuration of the CRM (e.g. Salesforce or HubSpot), including fields, workflows, user access, and reporting structure, in partnership with the RevOps or systems team. Drive adoption of CRM and sales processes by working with managers and reps, and by making the right behaviour the easy one. Support territory, quota, and compensation-related analysis as needed, in partnership with Finance. Identify process gaps and inefficiencies across the sales funnel and lead improvements, documenting changes and training the team on them. Work cross-functionally with Marketing, Finance, Customer Success, and Product Ops to keep data consistent across systems. What you’ll bring 7+ years of experience in sales operations, revenue operations, GTM operations, or a related commercial role, ideally in a [B2B SaaS / relevant industry] environment. Strong experience with CRM systems, ideally Salesforce or HubSpot, including reporting and basic administration. Solid understanding of sales metrics and funnel dynamics, including pipeline coverage, conversion, forecasting accuracy, and sales cycle length. Proven ability to build clear reports and dashboards in tools such as Excel/Google Sheets, Looker, Tableau, or Power BI. You don’t need to write code, but you should be comfortable working with data and spotting what matters. Experience running pipeline reviews or forecast calls, or supporting leaders who do. A consultative approach: you can listen to a sales leader, ask the right questions, and turn their needs into a practical solution. Strong communication skills, with the ability to present findings clearly to senior stakeholders and explain trade-offs simply. Good judgement and attention to detail, with the ability to balance speed and accuracy. Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment with multiple priorities. Nice to have Experience supporting a sales team through a scaling or transformation phase. Familiarity with sales compensation or territory planning tools. Exposure to revenue analytics or forecasting methodologies. Experience with a BI tool or basic SQL, though this is not required. What success looks like Leadership trusts the pipeline and forecast numbers and uses them to make decisions. Sales managers run their reviews from the dashboards you’ve built, without needing manual reports. CRM data quality improves measurably over time. Sales leaders see you as a partner who brings ideas, not just reports. About your application English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us. A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails. Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us. Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you. Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here . Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role. title: Sustainability solutions consultant (french & german speaking)
description: About Watershed Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team. We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us! The role We're looking for more early members to join our Sustainability solutions team! You may be a fit for this role if you’re excited to help Europe's largest companies deliver real decarbonisation, navigate an increasingly complex landscape of investor pressure, customer expectations and regulatory requirements. You’re willing to roll your sleeves up and go deep with prospective customers on their functional and technical needs, partnering with our sales, product and climate science teams along the way. You may be a carbon accounting aficionado or you may have never worked in climate before but have a passion for the subject; either way, you have a knack for quickly learning new, complex topics and distilling them for others. You will: Partner closely with 3-4 Account Executives, to analyse and understand customers’ businesses, climate ambitions and software needs Become a trusted advisor to our prospective customers—educating them about corporate climate commitments, carbon accounting, regulation/policy and the Watershed offering Build and share subject matter expertise on how the world’s largest companies can run successful climate programs Demonstrate Watershed’s unique value to prospective customers, through product demonstrations, ROI analysis and customer stories Creatively apply the Agentic AI capabilities of the Watershed platform to address innovative use cases Scope complex customer engagements as Watershed expands to new industries Interface with Customer Success and Sustainability Advisory teams to ensure smooth handovers from pre- to post-contract Collaborate with Watershed’s Engineering, Product and Marketing teams to continuously improve Watershed’s products and positioning It is a mandatory requirement to have business level French and German for this role You might be a fit if you: Have worked in a Solutions Consulting or Sales Engineering role for an Enterprise SaaS company Have partnered with Account Executives to scope successful engagements with mid-sized to large companies Master new concepts and technologies quickly Have exceptional communication and presentation skills; can engage deeply with both technical and business executive audiences Get energy from working across multiple projects concurrently and wearing many hats Are passionate about decarbonising diverse industries, from aviation to manufacturing to cloud computing Are excited to join a startup and are ready to take responsibility defining a new standard for climate and Sustainability AI programs around the world! Considered a “very nice to have” if you: Have a background in corporate climate programs or carbon accounting Have policy experience, especially in climate/sustainability/corporate reporting This role might include up to 25% travel. Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles) Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so. What’s the interview process like? It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process. What if I need accommodations for my interview? At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. title: Fractional Product Lead - 3 month contract
description: We're customer obsessed. We put the customer at the heart of everything we do - and we're looking for people who feel the same way. About Bike Club Bike Club is the easiest way to keep kids on the right sized bike. Through our subscription model, we remove the hassle of buying, outgrowing and reselling children's bikes, so families always have the right bike, right when they need it. We are a purpose led, fast-growing business built on ease, care, progress and joy - with a relentless focus on customer growth, retention and building a more circular approach to children's cycling. Role Summary and Engagement Bike Club is looking for a fractional Product Lead to lead the member product, turn customer needs and commercial priorities into a clear direction and a prioritised roadmap, and deliver measurable improvements. The role combines senior Product leadership with practical discovery and delivery coordination in a lean team. The Product Lead will also establish an AI-enabled Product function, using AI to speed up customer insight, discovery, prototyping and experimentation. They will identify where AI and automation can improve the member experience or business efficiency, and turn the strongest opportunities into prioritised, measurable initiatives. This is a part-time fixed-term employment or freelance contract estimated at 3 days per week for a period of 3 months. Key Responsibilities Product direction and roadmap: own the direction and roadmap across the member lifecycle: joining, managing a subscription, ongoing membership, exchange and retention. Balance member value with operational efficiency, cost and business priorities. Discovery: lead discovery with members and colleagues across Marketing, Customer Service, Operations and markets. Use research, behavioural data and service insight to define problems before committing to solutions. Lifecycle and retention: work jointly with Marketing and the retention owner on lifecycle journeys, retention initiatives, experiments and shared measures. Product owns the supporting experience and requirements. Marketing owns campaign and channel execution. Requirements and backlog: turn agreed priorities into clear requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria. Maintain one prioritised product backlog, including operational improvements and approved AI or automation initiatives. Investment cases: build proportionate cases for investment, setting out expected benefits, cost, dependencies and how outcomes will be measured. Recommend stopping or deferring work where value is insufficient. Delivery: agree delivery commitments with Engineering using realistic estimates and available capacity. Coordinate stakeholders, adoption and launches with the combined QA and Delivery role, keeping risks and changes visible. Marketing autonomy: support Marketing with appropriate content, landing-page and experimentation capabilities. Agree the boundary between the member product, CRM and support tools. AI in Product work: use AI routinely for research synthesis, analysis, requirements development, prototyping and experiment design, and validate findings against customer evidence. Prioritise valuable applications with Marketing, Customer Service, Operations and the Data and Automation function. Test assumptions and build proportionate business cases. Customer-service automation should support the wider member journey. Share responsibility with Marketing for using AI to support lifecycle insight, proposition testing and retention experiments, with agreed measures of customer and commercial impact. Leave things in a better state: because the engagement is part-time and time-limited, document the roadmap, backlog, ways of working and AI approach so the team can continue without the Product Lead, and hand over clearly at the end. Requirements Extensive Product Management experience including owning a digital product roadmap and delivering measurable customer and commercial improvements, preferably in a subscription, membership or related consumer business. Strong discovery skills, including customer interviews, journey mapping, data interpretation, problem definition and testing assumptions before investment. Commercial judgement: can compare value, effort, cost and risk, build practical investment cases and make clear prioritisation decisions. Ability to lead across functions, challenge senior stakeholders constructively and maintain focus when priorities compete. Experience working with Engineering, Design, Marketing, Customer Service and Operations through delivery, launch and continuous improvement. Demonstrable experience embedding AI into Product workflows, with examples of faster learning, better decisions or reduced effort. Able to distinguish valuable AI applications from features that add unnecessary complexity. Track record of working independently and effectively in a part-time, fractional or interim capacity, making visible progress in limited days a week. Able to start quickly, and leave behind clear documentation and repeatable ways of working. Measures Of Success Baselines, numerical targets, data sources and review dates are agreed with the executive sponsor and relevant business owners within the first 30 days. Delivery and outcomes are reviewed weekly. Member retention: improvement in the agreed retention or cancellation measure for targeted journeys, assessed jointly with Marketing and the retention owner. Member experience: improvement in self-service completion and reduction in avoidable support contact for prioritised journeys, without deterioration in customer experience. Conversion: improvement in agreed joining and exchange conversion measures, using experiments or comparable cohorts where practical. Speed of learning: reduced time from identifying a customer problem to testing a solution, with evidence that decisions remain grounded in customer insight. AI and automation: validated initiatives deliver agreed improvements in member experience, retention or operational efficiency, measured with the relevant business owner. Roadmap value: proportion of priority initiatives with a stated outcome, baseline and measurement plan before delivery, followed by a documented benefits review. Delivery confidence: performance against jointly agreed milestones, with changes in scope, priorities and dependencies recorded and communicated early. Our Values We look for people who live our values every day: Ease: we make things simple for our members and for each other. Care: we look after our customers, our colleagues and our bikes. Progress: we keep improving, learning and raising the bar. Joy: we help kids fall in love with cycling, and enjoy the work we do. Why Bike Club? You'll be joining a business with a clear purpose, a genuinely different proposition and significant opportunity to grow. This is a rare opportunity to build the operating system for our national refurbishment and distribution site from the ground up, shaping how Bike Club gets the right bike to every family, right when they need it. What You Must Have Full account lifecycle ownership: +5 years of experience owning the commercial lifecycle of strategic or enterprise customer accounts, including retention, renewals, expansion, upselling, and cross-selling in a B2B SaaS environment. Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to collaborate effectively across a remote, international organisation. Experience engaging and influencing C-level and senior stakeholders, including the ability to lead strategic conversations and align solutions with business priorities. As our regional technical authority, you will establish scalable, repeatable controls solutions while ensuring they meet the demands of complex, mission-critical projects. This is a high-impact role combining regional strategy with practical engineering leadership. You will influence technical decisions from concept and detailed design through construction, commissioning, Integrated Systems Testing (IST) and operational handover, working alongside delivery teams, contractors and customers. You will also lead a small regional specialist team and support multiple projects across Europe. Key Responsibilities · Act as STACK’s EMEA technical authority for BMS, controls and automation, challenging designs and advising project teams, customers and delivery partners. · Own the development and continuous improvement of a standardised, scalable EMEA BMS product, including regional specifications, control philosophies and engineering standards. · Define repeatable system architectures, sequences of operation, hardware and software, networks, communications, graphics, alarms and equipment interfaces, with appropriate resilience and cybersecurity. · Adapt standards to local regulations and customer requirements, driving reliability, maintainability, innovation, delivery efficiency and cost optimisation. · Provide end-to-end technical oversight across multiple Data Centre projects, from concept and detailed design through construction, integration, commissioning, IST and operational handover. · Review and approve controls designs, drawings, technical submissions and specifications; ensure effective integration with mechanical, electrical and other critical infrastructure. · Oversee consultants, contractors and specialist suppliers; identify and mitigate design, programme, integration and commissioning risks, supporting customer acceptance and Ready for Service (RFS). · Establish commissioning procedures and acceptance criteria; oversee Level 3, 4 and 5 testing where applicable, including functional scripts and failure scenarios under normal and abnormal conditions. · Provide hands-on troubleshooting, root cause analysis and technical support for complex controls and communications issues, including chilled water systems, chillers, pumps, valves and free cooling. · Capture lessons learned and improve future designs, standards and operational performance. · Lead and develop a small regional specialist team, balancing resources and priorities across projects and supporting recruitment and succession planning. · Work closely with engineering, construction, commissioning, operations, commercial and global technical teams; build supplier relationships and report risks and technical performance to senior leaders. What You’ll Bring · Extensive experience in controls engineering, BMS or industrial automation, with a strong hands-on background in programming, integration, engineering or commissioning. · Significant delivery experience in hyperscale Data Centre's or comparable mission-critical environments, from design through construction, commissioning, IST and handover. · Experience establishing technical standards, control philosophies and repeatable engineering solutions, alongside the judgement to balance strategy with practical delivery. · Deep technical expertise in BMS, PLCs, DDC controllers, SCADA, controls logic, sequences of operation and system integration. · Strong knowledge of Data Centre mechanical and electrical systems, particularly chilled water plant, chiller sequencing, pump controls and free cooling. · Knowledge of BMS architecture, networks, resilience, cybersecurity, BACnet, Modbus, OPC UA and relevant communications protocols. · Experience with functional testing, failure scenario validation, alarm management, trending and operational performance optimisation; familiarity with ASHRAE, EN 50600, IEC and applicable local standards. · Proven ability to lead specialist teams and contractors across locations, solve complex technical problems and influence senior stakeholders with sound commercial judgement. · A degree or equivalent qualification in Electrical Engineering, Controls, Automation, Mechatronics or a related field, or substantial equivalent practical experience. Professional accreditation or relevant certifications are advantageous. What We Offer · The opportunity to shape engineering standards and controls delivery across a growing portfolio of critical Data Centre infrastructure. · A chance to build your career with STACK, working alongside experienced technical and delivery teams across EMEA. · Competitive benefits aligned with local country policies. About STACK Infrastructure STACK is a proven, trusted partner for the world’s most innovative companies, designing, developing, and operating sustainable global digital infrastructure. Backed by an unmatched record of reliable delivery and development expertise, STACK brings speed, scale, certainty, and responsibility to the demands of a rapidly evolving digital infrastructure landscape. title: Inventory Specialist
description: The opportunity We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with ownership and a direct line to the founders. Youʼll help make sure laboratory teams have the consumables they need, when they need them. Youʼll have a say in the software they use to manage stock, and learn to use AI to make everyday purchasing and inventory work easier. About us AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one. We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team. The role This is a hands-on, early-career role within our Infrastructure team. Youʼll manage day-to-day consumables purchasing, receive deliveries and keep stock records accurate, with training and guidance from your manager and laboratory colleagues. As you learn the work, youʼll organise your day independently and follow issues through to resolution. Youʼll work with laboratory teams to understand demand, place orders within agreed budgets and approvals, and chase delays before they disrupt work. Youʼll maintain supplier prices and lead times, flag supply risks and get laboratory approval for any proposed substitutions. At goods receipt, youʼll check orders against deliveries, including quantities, condition and relevant batch, expiry and temperature requirements. Youʼll record receipts promptly, route goods to the right storage and resolve discrepancies. Youʼll help physically set up storage areas, organise stock into defined bin locations and label and barcode those locations so they match the inventory records. Youʼll record stock movements and investigate differences found during stock counts. With guidance, youʼll propose reorder points and buffer stock using consumption, lead times and planned activity. Youʼll track expiry dates, prioritise the earliest-expiring stock where appropriate and maintain consistent item codes, units and pack conversions. Youʼll document procedures, follow safety and quality requirements, and segregate items awaiting review. Regular updates on supply risks and stock accuracy, together with reliable receipt records, will help colleagues in the lab and finance. Youʼll work directly with software engineers to shape the inventory tools you use every day. Youʼll bring ideas from the lab, explain what needs to work differently and test new features against real tasks. Your input will help decide what gets improved, with your manager and the software team leading priorities, design and development. Youʼll also learn to use AI-assisted workflows for tasks such as reviewing inventory data and preparing routine updates, then help refine those workflows as you find better ways to work. Training and support will be part of the role. Your first 90 days FIRST 30 DAYS ◆ Learn the consumables, storage requirements and approval processes with laboratory colleagues. Take on routine ordering and goods receipt with support. ◆ Check stock records against physical inventory and map the journey from purchase request to use. Agree a practical storage layout and bin-location scheme with laboratory colleagues, taking account of access and storage requirements. DAYS 30 TO 60 ◆ Run routine ordering, receipts and stock counts independently within agreed processes. Keep colleagues informed of shortages, overdue orders and expiring stock. ◆ Physically set up and organise the agreed storage areas, label and barcode bin locations, and link them to inventory records. Propose replenishment settings with your manager and laboratory colleagues, and document how stock is stored and moved. Turn recurring problems into examples for the software team. DAYS 60 TO 90 ◆ Check that colleagues can find, receive and return stock using the labelled and barcoded locations. Resolve gaps in the layout or records, and refine replenishment to reduce avoidable shortages and waste. ◆ Test available inventory features against everyday tasks and help colleagues adopt improvements. With support, try an AI-assisted workflow for a routine task, check its outputs and suggest how to improve it. Who you are Youʼre proactive, organised and attentive to detail, and you enjoy practical work where accurate records have visible consequences. When a problem arises, you flag it promptly and investigate practical solutions while keeping colleagues informed. You act within agreed processes, bring options when a decision needs support and follow the issue through to resolution. Your experience may come from inventory, purchasing, logistics or laboratory operations, including an apprenticeship or placement. A scientific degree and coding experience are not required. We welcome transferable experience with physical stock and time-sensitive supplies. Youʼre willing to help beyond a fixed task list as the team grows, while using judgement about when to escalate. Nobody arrives with every part of this role. If you are strong in most of it and quick to learn the rest, we want to hear from you. MUST HAVE ◆ Practical experience of inventory, purchasing, goods receipt, logistics or laboratory operations. ◆ Careful record-keeping and an organised approach to checking deliveries, prioritising work and following actions through. ◆ Confidence with digital tools and a willingness to learn to use AI, check its outputs and improve recurring workflows over time. Prior AI expertise is not required. ◆ Clear communication with suppliers and colleagues, including explaining an operational problem to a software developer. NICE TO HAVE ◆ Experience with laboratory consumables or expiry-sensitive and temperature-controlled stock. ◆ Familiarity with inventory or ERP systems, barcode-based stock control, or testing new software. Why this is unusual Alongside keeping supplies moving, youʼll help shape the software and AI-assisted workflows that make the job easier. Youʼll work with engineers to turn a stock discrepancy or awkward receiving step into a better tool, then see whether it works in practice. Youʼll build experience in improving systems as well as running the day-to-day operation. Youʼll have support as you learn, and room to contribute ideas from the start. Some people find that mix energising; others prefer a more settled routine. It is worth knowing which suits you. How we work This role is primarily on-site in Kingʼs Cross, London, typically four to five days a week, because deliveries and physical inventory need someone there. The wider team is distributed, so we write things down and keep colleagues informed. We start the week with an all-hands and share written updates. We give feedback directly and expect good ideas to be challenged on their merits, whoever proposes them. UK benefits include 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution after a three-month deferment, and Bupa private health cover. The team you will join Youʼll join the Infrastructure team and work closely with laboratory colleagues, software engineers and finance. Your manager will help set priorities and support decisions on inventory planning and wider process changes. Youʼll bring the day-to-day operational view into those discussions. Our process We start with a short screening conversation, followed by a behavioural interview. Weʼll ask for examples of how youʼve spotted a problem, kept others informed and taken practical steps to solve it, including when you sought support. Next comes a role-specific work sample and a discussion of how you approached it, followed by references. Weʼll explain the assessment format in advance, and youʼll meet us in person before any offer. If the role interests you, apply through the person who introduced you or the recruiter who shared it. If youʼre unsure whether you meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. We are an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background. title: Product Lead
description: About Abound We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation. And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch. Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us. The Role We are hiring a Product Lead to own our Express / Mid-prime personal loan product, one of our highest-priority growth areas. This is unsecured personal lending in the higher-APR mid-prime space (30% to 50% APR), with loans typically from £2,000 to £10,000, and customers acquired primarily through price-comparison and aggregator marketplaces. Our ambition is to grow this product many times over while improving its economics, and this role owns the product that makes that happen. This is a product role first. You will own the Express/Mid-prime proposition end to end: who we serve, how we quote and present offers on marketplaces, how the journey converts, how we price, and how the product performs once the loans are on the book. What makes it different from a typical product role is that the product is credit. The levers that drive growth, such as eligibility, pricing, offer design and underwriting, are the same levers that drive loss rates, so you need to be comfortable working with risk and data science rather than handing that part off. We think this is a great role for someone with around four to five years of experience who has built a strong foundation in lending or fintech, has worked hands-on with data and credit decisioning, and is ready to own a product outright rather than a slice of one. You will set the direction for the segment, run the roadmap, and be accountable for the results, with the backing of experienced risk, data science and commercial leaders around you. Our decisioning is built on Open Banking and cashflow underwriting rather than credit scores alone. For a higher-APR population acquired through marketplaces, seeing real affordability is what lets us select and price better than the market. The interesting product problem is that richer data comes at a cost to conversion, so the job is to capture that data advantage while designing a journey and offer that customers actually complete. The defining challenge is balance: scaling volume by an order of magnitude while building a book of genuinely good credit quality. The best people in this space know that those two goals can be reconciled rather than traded off, and are curious enough to work out how. What you'll be doing Own the Express / Mid-prime product: proposition, roadmap, performance and economics, with direct accountability for the balance between growth and credit quality. Lead how we quote and present offers across aggregator and price-comparison marketplaces, optimising eligibility, risk-based pricing and offer presentation to win the right customers at the point of acquisition. Own conversion through the journey, from quote to disbursal, including how we ask customers for Open Banking data and how that affects drop-off and the quality of the book. Understand and actively manage adverse selection in marketplace-acquired lending, shaping offer, pricing and decisioning strategy to attract the customers we want and screen out the risk we do not. Work with data science to make sure our credit models are calibrated and tuned for this population rather than inherited unchanged from prime or adjacent segments, and be able to get into the data yourself when needed. Use credit and commercial insight to optimise unit economics, balancing approval rates, pricing, loss rates and volume so the product scales profitably. Monitor product and portfolio performance across the customer lifecycle, spotting emerging trends, risks and opportunities early. Shape underwriting strategy, segmentation, credit policy and decisioning logic in partnership with risk and data science. Design and evaluate experiments and strategy changes, and turn the analysis into clear, actionable recommendations. Own the management information for the segment: define the metrics, monitoring and reporting that let the business make consistent decisions about the product. Assess new initiatives, customer segments and product changes with both a commercial and a credit lens. Present clear, structured updates on product performance to senior leadership and governance forums, and support funding and due diligence conversations where the product is in focus. Who you are A product person at heart: you care about the customer, the journey and the commercial outcome, and you want to own something end to end. Quantitative and hands-on. You are comfortable in SQL and Python (or similar), you can interrogate a dataset yourself, and you can hold your own in a conversation with data scientists about model performance and calibration. Credit-literate. You understand how eligibility, pricing and underwriting decisions shape the book you end up with, and you have a working understanding of adverse selection and why it matters in marketplace lending. Commercially sharp, with a solid grasp of unit economics and a clear understanding that product decisions in lending have to work for both growth and portfolio performance. Curious about trade-offs rather than defensive about them: alert to the fact that deeper affordability assessment can hurt conversion, and motivated by the challenge of capturing its value without sacrificing growth. Able to move between detail and direction: happy getting into the data on a Tuesday and shaping the roadmap on a Wednesday. Confident challenging assumptions and turning analysis into practical action, and able to explain your reasoning clearly to people who are not analysts. Collaborative and credible with risk, commercial, engineering and data science teams. Structured, proactive and comfortable in a scaling environment where priorities evolve quickly and ownership is expected. Experience and background Around four to five years of experience in product, credit strategy, analytics or a closely related role within consumer lending or fintech. We are deliberately targeting this level: this is a step-up role for someone ready to own a product, not a lateral move for someone who has run several. Experience in unsecured consumer lending, ideally Unsecured Personal Loans (UPL), with exposure to the mechanics of acquiring customers through price-comparison or aggregator marketplaces. Direct experience in higher-APR or near-prime lending is a strong plus but not a prerequisite. Hands-on data skills: SQL as a minimum, and ideally Python or R for analysis. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you need to be able to work alongside them as a peer and do your own analysis. Experience working with or alongside credit decisioning, scorecards or risk models, and an understanding of how they are built, monitored and adjusted for a specific population. Some experience of pricing, eligibility or offer design, and of using experiments or A/B tests to evaluate changes. A track record of using analysis to influence decisions, not just to report on outcomes, in a role where you had some accountability for commercial results. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present clearly to senior stakeholders. Experience with Open Banking data or cashflow underwriting is a plus, as is experience in a fast-growing fintech. What we offer: Everyone owns a piece of the company - equity Hybrid with 3 days a week in the office 25 days’ holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays 2 paid volunteering days per year One month paid sabbatical after 4 years Employee loan Free gym membership Team wellness budget to be active together - set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Commercial Lead - Clinical Trials
description: We’re Heidi. We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties. Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart. We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again. We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years. To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund. If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in. The role We are hiring a Clinical Trials Lead to own the commercial work that follows. You will develop Heidi’s view of the market, identify the strongest entry point, build senior relationships across the industry, secure early customers and shape a repeatable route to market. Your knowledge of clinical trials will inform and shape what Heidi builds. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who operates like a founder. You will make the calls, open the doors, write the proposal, run the meeting and stay accountable after the contract is signed. As the business proves itself, the role can grow into broader ownership of Heidi’s clinical trials business. What you’ll do Develop the market thesis. Map the clinical trials ecosystem, test the most valuable opportunities and recommend where Heidi should focus its time and capital. Lead customer development. Build direct relationships with senior decision makers across sponsors, biotechnology companies, CROs, sites and health systems. Conduct the outreach yourself and turn conversations into qualified opportunities. Own early commercial outcomes. Build the pipeline, secure design partners and paid programmes, and own early revenue. Define the measures that show whether the business is gaining traction. Shape the proposition. Turn buyer needs into a clear commercial offer, including target customer, value proposition, pricing, packaging and proof of value. Inform what Heidi builds. Bring evidence from customers and clinical trials workflows to the product lead. Help the team choose problems worth solving while the product lead retains ownership of product strategy and delivery. Navigate the buying process. Understand how life sciences organisations evaluate vendors, allocate budgets, manage procurement and compliance, and move from pilot to broader deployment. Build the delivery model. Work with product, engineering, clinical, legal and implementation colleagues to make early programmes successful and increasingly repeatable. Create the route to scale. Determine which partnerships, channels, proof points and team capabilities are required to grow beyond founder-led selling. Represent Heidi. Build Heidi’s credibility with customers, partners and industry networks through thoughtful engagement and useful domain expertise. What you’ll need The strongest candidates will combine deep clinical trials knowledge with a record of creating commercial value. We expect the following experience. Deep experience in the clinical trials industry through a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company, CRO, trial technology business, research network or closely related organisation. A strong understanding of how clinical trials are funded, sold, bought and delivered, including the incentives and constraints faced by sponsors, CROs and research sites. A record of building revenue, partnerships, a business line or a company in the sector. You can show what you personally originated and how it performed. Senior commercial credibility. You can open a conversation with an industry executive, diagnose the underlying business problem and move the relationship towards a concrete commitment. The judgement to operate in a regulated environment while respecting Good Clinical Practice, patient consent, privacy and data integrity. The independence to create structure, make decisions and produce results without an established playbook or a large supporting team. Passion for AI, shown through hands-on building, prototyping, or side projects. You default to building over requesting. You're confident in your thinking and open to being wrong. Great ideas win regardless of who surfaces them. How we show up Build for the next decade, not next quarter . Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism. Lead, don't wait . We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that. Follow the evidence . Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford. Own the outcome . Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander. Ship, measure, go again . A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless. Live in clinicians' reality . Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it. Why Heidi? You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver. Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally. We take care of you. title: Staff Engineer, EU Infrastructure
description: About Wolt At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe. Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life. About the Team Our Infrastructure teams build the foundation that engineers at Wolt, Deliveroo, and DoorDash build on: the compute, cloud, and networking capabilities that enable Engineering teams to develop, deploy, and run services at global scale. The EU Compute team has a specific focus on provisioning, scaling, and the efficient operation of GPU infrastructure for AI and ML workloads. This is an emerging space with plenty of greenfield opportunities. We're looking for a Staff Engineer to be a hands-on technical leader for this infrastructure work that crosses team and brand boundaries. You'll set direction for the platform, turn complex problems into deliverable plans, write and review production code, and help other engineers make sound decisions. It's an exciting time to join: we're building a global platform and the choices made now will shape how engineers across the company ship for years. What you'll be doing You'll own some of the hardest infrastructure problems in the company and make the platform easier to operate and safer to build on. We're determined to build great platform products and user experiences, and you'll be pivotal in making this reality. Day-to-day in this role you'll: Set technical direction for shared AWS and Kubernetes infrastructure, balancing reliability, security, developer experience, and cost. Lead substantial initiatives from design through rollout and operation, coordinating dependencies and decisions across Wolt, Deliveroo and DoorDash, focusing on workloads targeting GPUs. Evolve Kubernetes clusters, cloud networking, identity, and infrastructure provisioning to support growing and varied workloads. Build reusable Terraform patterns and self-service tooling that help teams provision infrastructure safely and consistently. Improve deployment and operational practices, including GitOps, observability, capacity planning, incident response and recovery. Use production signals and developer feedback to find platform friction, choose where to invest and measure whether changes actually help. Assist with supporting the platform, with deep focus on GPU infrastructure, as well as broad focus on compute in general. Gracefully sunset legacy infrastructure and tooling, and create strategies to reduce toil. Mentor engineers through design reviews, implementation and incidents, raising the quality of infrastructure work across teams. Our humble expectations Deep experience building and operating Kubernetes and AWS infrastructure in production. Familiarity with GPU workloads and orchestration is a plus. Strong software engineering skills: you use Go, Python or a similar language to build maintainable tools and automation. Experience with infrastructure as code (we use Terraform) and with designing systems that other engineering teams depend on. A track record of leading complex technical work across teams, including architectural decisions, delivery, and operational follow-through. You have the breadth to collaborate and design across team and domain boundaries, and the depth to have hands-on impact. Strong judgment on trade-offs in distributed systems, networking, security, reliability, and cloud cost. Clear communication, and the ability to bring people together around a practical technical direction. What we offer Scope and influence. Shape infrastructure used globally, while staying close to the engineering. Your work will help product teams ship services with greater ease and confidence. Real problems at global scale. Multi-cluster Kubernetes, AI / ML workloads, cloud networking, GitOps, and progressive delivery across a global company. Autonomy and ownership. Set direction and see it through from design to operation, with the backing of a global engineering organisation spanning Europe and the US. Growth. Room to expand your scope, whether through deeper technical leadership or broader cross-domain influence. Great people. Work with talented engineers and leaders in a diverse, international environment, mentoring and learning from others. Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel. title: Golang Backend Engineer, Financial Product Fraud
description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person. We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform. This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch. We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one. This role will be based in London , UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin. What you'll do: Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers. Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout. Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times. Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer. Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter. Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team. Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event. Our expectations: 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production. 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly. A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one. Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar). Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability. Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality. Nice to have Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud. Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path. Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go. Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP). Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes. What we value A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output. Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them. A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments. Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together. An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong. We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief. If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience. If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you! title: Field Marketing Manager - Net New EMEA (DAM)
description: About Us: At Sitecore, our mission is to simplify how brands reach, engage, and serve people by delivering intelligent, personalised digital experiences that connect the world. We empower the world’s most iconic brands to build lifelong relationships with their customers—seamlessly, smartly, and at scale. As the leading provider of agentic digital experience software, Sitecore brings together content, commerce, and data into one composable platform that enables brands to deliver millions of meaningful, adaptive experiences every day. Trusted by global leaders such as American Express, Porsche, Starbucks, and L’Oréal, Sitecore helps brands transform engagement through experiences that are not only personalised but predictive and dynamic. Our foundation is our people—a diverse, passionate, and collaborative global team spanning over 25 countries. We believe that every experience matters, and that belief starts with how we work together. Our values—empathy, accountability, clarity, and growth—guide how we lead, innovate, and connect. They are the behaviours that bring our mission and vision to life, every day, in every interaction. As we continue to evolve, we are actively cultivating AI skills across our teams to unlock new levels of creativity, efficiency, and insight. From engineering to customer experience, AI capabilities are becoming integral to how we design, build, and deliver the next generation of digital experiences. Learn more at Sitecore.com About the Role: Sitecore is seeking a dynamic and results-driven Field Marketing Manager to lead Net New demand generation for Digital Asset Management (DAM) across EMEA. This role will build market awareness, create qualified pipeline, and accelerate new customer acquisition through integrated field marketing aligned with regional go-to-market priorities. You will develop and execute multi-channel programs that bring the DAM value proposition to target accounts and priority industries. Working closely with the DAM team, regional sales, business development, product marketing, and campaigns, you will turn audience and market insight into measurable pipeline. The ideal candidate is entrepreneurial, commercially minded, data-driven, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. What You Will Do: Strategy & Planning Define and execute the Net New DAM demand generation strategy for EMEA, aligned with regional GTM, account priorities, and growth objectives Build integrated field marketing plans that increase DAM awareness, engage buying groups, and convert priority accounts Pipeline Generation Deliver qualified DAM pipeline targets alongside regional sales leadership, business development, and the DAM team Use account, intent, and market data to identify high-potential audiences, industries, and buying signals across EMEA Field Marketing Programs Design and deliver high-impact regional programs aligned with sales priorities, target account needs, and local market opportunities Create connected journeys across events, digital activation, executive engagement, and sales follow-up to move accounts through the funnel Campaign Execution Localize and activate global DAM campaigns, adapting the value proposition, messaging, content, and tactics for EMEA audiences Own the execution of field events, webinars, executive programs, and digital campaigns that support Net New DAM acquisition Performance & Optimization Track and report campaign engagement, sourced and stakeholder feedback Collaboration & Enablement Collaborate with the DAM team, Corporate Marketing, Product Marketing, Regional Sales, Business Development, and Sales Enablement to align plans and resources Act as a trusted marketing advisor to sales teams, equipping them with DAM messaging, campaign plays, and timely follow-up guidance What You Need to Succeed: A minimum of 5 years of B2B marketing experience, ideally in SaaS, enterprise software, digital experience, content operations, or DAM Proven success in field marketing with responsibility for Net New pipeline creation across multiple EMEA markets Strong understanding of account-based marketing, buying groups, intent data, demand generation, and funnel acceleration Experience designing and executing integrated field programs that engage target accounts and accelerate pipeline; DAM or content technology experience is advantageous Excellent communication, program management, and stakeholder management skills across regional and global teams Proficiency in marketing automation, CRM, account intelligence, and analytics platforms Fluent in English; additional European languages and experience marketing across
